# Terraform AWS SSM Compliance Management Module

 [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-ssm-compliance-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-ssm-compliance-management/releases/latest) [![Last Updated](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-ssm-compliance-management.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-ssm-compliance-management/commits)


Terraform module for the account- and Region-level AWS Systems Manager resources that support AWS Security Hub CSPM controls SSM.1 through SSM.7. It manages Default Host Management Configuration, Inventory, patch compliance scans, patch baselines and groups, State Manager associations, private and tagged SSM documents, Automation logging, public document-sharing prevention, and Maintenance Windows. Session Manager resources are intentionally excluded.


---

## Introduction

This module establishes a Systems Manager compliance baseline without managing Session Manager preferences,
session documents, interactive access, RDP, SSH, or session audit logging.

Safe account-level controls are enabled by default:

- Default Host Management Configuration and its IAM service role.
- Daily `AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory` collection for all managed nodes.
- Daily, non-rebooting `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` scan operations for all managed nodes.
- CloudWatch Logs delivery settings for Automation customer-script output.
- Prevention of new public SSM document sharing.

Patch installation, custom patch baselines, resource data sync, customer-owned documents, additional
State Manager associations, and Maintenance Windows are opt-in because they require deployment-specific
schedules, targets, permissions, or storage destinations.

## Security Hub CSPM control coverage

| Control | Module responsibility | Runtime responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSM.1 | Enables Default Host Management Configuration and creates or references its IAM role. | Instances must meet Systems Manager managed-node prerequisites and successfully register. |
| SSM.2 | Creates a scheduled patch compliance scan and optionally manages patch baselines, groups, and install windows. | Nodes must execute scans and installations successfully; missing or failed patches still produce findings. |
| SSM.3 | Creates Inventory, patch scan, and caller-defined State Manager associations with compliance reporting. | Associations must execute successfully on every targeted managed node. |
| SSM.4 | Blocks future public sharing and creates module-owned documents without public sharing. | Existing public documents must be identified and unshared before or during adoption. |
| SSM.5 | Applies the module's standard tags plus document-specific tags to every module-owned document. | Existing documents outside this module remain the caller's responsibility. |
| SSM.6 | Configures Automation customer-script logging to a CloudWatch Logs group. | Automation runbooks and IAM roles must permit their expected logging and workload operations. |
| SSM.7 | Sets the account/Region public-sharing permission to `Disable`. | The setting prevents new public shares but does not remove shares created previously. |

Security Hub findings are based on observed AWS resource and execution state. A successful Terraform
apply provides the required configuration but cannot guarantee that managed nodes remain online or that
every association and patch operation succeeds.

## Usage



The module accepts one structured `settings` object. With an empty object it applies the safe baseline
described above. Disable or narrow an individual default explicitly when adopting an account with
existing associations.

```hcl
module "ssm_compliance" {
  source  = "cloudopsworks/ssm-compliance-management/aws"
  version = "~> 1.0"

  org = {
    organization_name = "example"
    organization_unit = "platform"
    environment_type  = "production"
    environment_name  = "shared"
  }

  settings = {
    inventory = {
      enabled  = true
      schedule = "rate(1 day)"
      targets = [{
        key    = "tag:SSMManaged"
        values = ["true"]
      }]
    }

    patch_scan = {
      enabled  = true
      schedule = "rate(1 day)"
      targets = [{
        key    = "tag:Patch Group"
        values = ["amazon-linux"]
      }]
    }

    patch_baselines = {
      amazon_linux = {
        operating_system = "AMAZON_LINUX_2"
        approval_rules = [{
          approve_after_days = 7
          compliance_level   = "HIGH"
          patch_filters = [{
            key    = "CLASSIFICATION"
            values = ["Security"]
          }]
        }]
      }
    }

    patch_groups = {
      amazon_linux = {
        patch_group  = "amazon-linux"
        baseline_key = "amazon_linux"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Adopt an existing Inventory association

AWS permits only one apply-all `AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory` association in an account and Region.
Find the existing association UUID before the first apply:

```sh
aws ssm list-associations \
  --association-filter-list key=Name,value=AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory \
  --query 'Associations[].{AssociationId:AssociationId,AssociationName:AssociationName,Targets:Targets}' \
  --output table
```

For the generated Terragrunt scaffold, set the UUID in `inputs.yaml`:

```yaml
settings:
  inventory:
    enabled: true
    existing_association_id: 10abcdef-0abc-1234-5678-90abcdef1234
```

The scaffold generates a root-level declarative import for
`aws_ssm_association.inventory[0]`. The first plan should show one import instead of one add.
Keep the configured schedule, targets, parameters, and association name aligned with the existing
association if it must not be updated after adoption. Terraform 1.5 or newer or OpenTofu 1.6 or newer
is required for configuration-driven import.

For an existing Terragrunt folder that has not been regenerated from the updated scaffold, perform
the equivalent one-time import directly:

```sh
terragrunt import \
  'aws_ssm_association.inventory[0]' \
  '10abcdef-0abc-1234-5678-90abcdef1234'
```

Direct module callers can add the import block in their root module:

```hcl
import {
  to = module.ssm_compliance.aws_ssm_association.inventory[0]
  id = "10abcdef-0abc-1234-5678-90abcdef1234"
}
```

Or perform the equivalent one-time state import:

```sh
tofu import \
  'module.ssm_compliance.aws_ssm_association.inventory[0]' \
  '10abcdef-0abc-1234-5678-90abcdef1234'
```

### Complete annotated settings reference

The Terragrunt scaffold generates this fully annotated `inputs.yaml`. Active values show the safe
baseline; every optional override and nested resource option is included as a comment.

```yaml
# Module configuration
#
# Every supported settings option is shown below. Safe defaults are active; optional
# features and overrides remain commented. Review target overlap before applying to an
# account that already has Systems Manager associations.
settings:
  # Default Host Management Configuration (Security Hub SSM.1).
  default_host_management:
    enabled: true                                # Enable the account/Region service setting. Default: true
    create_role: true                            # Create the IAM role named below. Default: true
    # role_name: AWSSystemsManagerDefaultEC2InstanceManagementRole # Existing or created role name.
    # role_path: /service-role/                   # IAM path, including leading/trailing slash. Default: /service-role/
    # additional_policy_arns: []                 # Extra managed policies attached only when create_role is true.

  # Automation customer-script logging (Security Hub SSM.6).
  automation_logging:
    enabled: true                                # Configure both Automation logging service settings. Default: true
    create_log_group: true                       # Create the namespaced group; set false when another module owns log-group lifecycle. Default: true
    # log_group_name: /aws/ssm/compliance-management/automation/example # Created or pre-existing group name. Default uses the module-specific namespace shown here.
    retention_in_days: 365                       # CloudWatch retention when creating the group. Default: 365
    # kms_key_id: null                           # Optional KMS key ARN for CloudWatch Logs encryption.
    # skip_destroy: false                        # Retain the log group during destroy. Default: false

  # SSM document account controls (Security Hub SSM.4 and SSM.7).
  document_security:
    block_public_sharing: true                   # Set public-sharing-permission to Disable. Default: true

  # Systems Manager Inventory association.
  inventory:
    enabled: true                                # Create AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory. Default: true
    # existing_association_id: 10abcdef-0abc-1234-5678-90abcdef1234 # Existing association UUID to import through the generated Terragrunt configuration.
    # association_name: ssm-inventory-example    # Default: ssm-inventory-<system-name>
    schedule: rate(1 day)                        # Rate or cron expression. Default: rate(1 day)
    # apply_only_at_cron_interval: false         # Wait for the first schedule instead of running on apply. Default: false
    # max_concurrency: "10%"                     # Optional node concurrency number or percentage.
    # max_errors: "1"                            # Optional tolerated error number or percentage.
    # compliance_severity: MEDIUM                # CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or UNSPECIFIED. Default: MEDIUM
    # wait_for_success_timeout_seconds: null      # Optional provider wait timeout.
    targets:                                     # Up to five State Manager target blocks.
      - key: InstanceIds                         # Examples: InstanceIds, tag:Environment, resource-groups:Name.
        values: ["*"]                            # Default targets every managed node.
    # parameters:                                # Overrides merged with the Inventory defaults below.
    #   applications: Enabled                    # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   awsComponents: Enabled                   # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   customInventory: Enabled                 # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   instanceDetailedInformation: Enabled     # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   networkConfig: Enabled                   # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   services: Enabled                        # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   windowsRoles: Enabled                    # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   windowsUpdates: Enabled                  # Enabled or Disabled. Default: Enabled
    #   files: '[]'                              # Optional AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory files JSON string.
    #   windowsRegistry: '[]'                    # Optional Windows registry inventory JSON string.
    # resource_data_sync:                        # Optional Inventory export to an existing S3 bucket.
    #   enabled: false                           # Default: false
    #   name: inventory-sync                     # Default: ssm-inventory-<short-system-name>
    #   bucket_name: existing-inventory-bucket   # Required when enabled; this module does not create the bucket.
    #   prefix: inventory                        # S3 key prefix. Default: inventory
    #   region: us-east-1                        # Bucket Region. Default: current provider Region
    #   sync_format: JsonSerDe                   # SSM Inventory sync format. Default: JsonSerDe
    #   kms_key_arn: null                        # Optional KMS key ARN used by the destination.

  # Non-rebooting patch compliance scan association (Security Hub SSM.2/SSM.3).
  patch_scan:
    enabled: true                                # Create AWS-RunPatchBaseline with Operation=Scan. Default: true
    # association_name: ssm-patch-scan-example   # Default: ssm-patch-scan-<system-name>
    schedule: rate(1 day)                        # Rate or cron expression. Default: rate(1 day)
    # apply_only_at_cron_interval: false         # Wait for the first schedule instead of running on apply. Default: false
    compliance_severity: HIGH                    # CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or UNSPECIFIED. Default: HIGH
    # max_concurrency: "10%"                     # Node concurrency number or percentage. Default: 10%
    # max_errors: "1"                            # Tolerated error number or percentage. Default: 1
    # wait_for_success_timeout_seconds: null      # Optional provider wait timeout.
    targets:                                     # Up to five State Manager target blocks.
      - key: InstanceIds
        values: ["*"]                            # Default targets every managed node.

  # Customer-owned SSM documents. Session documents are rejected by this module.
  # documents:
  #   example:                                   # Arbitrary stable map key.
  #     name: ExampleDocument                    # Default: <system-name>-<map-key>
  #     document_type: Command                   # Any AWS-supported type except Session. Default: Command
  #     document_format: YAML                    # YAML, JSON, or TEXT as supported by the document type. Default: YAML
  #     content: |-                              # Required document body.
  #       schemaVersion: '2.2'
  #       description: Example command document
  #       mainSteps: []
  #     target_type: /AWS::EC2::Instance         # Optional document target type.
  #     version_name: v1                         # Optional friendly document version name.
  #     shared_account_ids: []                   # Private 12-digit AWS account IDs only; public "All" is rejected.
  #     tags: {}                                 # Merged over the module standard tags.
  #     attachments_source:                      # Optional document attachment sources, up to twenty.
  #       - key: SourceUrl                       # SourceUrl, S3FileUrl, or AttachmentReference.
  #         name: null                           # Optional attachment name.
  #         values: ["https://example.invalid"]  # Values accepted by the selected attachment key.

  # Additional State Manager associations (Security Hub SSM.3).
  # associations:
  #   update_agent:                              # Arbitrary stable map key.
  #     name: AWS-UpdateSSMAgent                 # Required AWS-managed or customer document name.
  #     association_name: update-ssm-agent       # Default: <system-name>-<map-key>
  #     document_version: "$LATEST"              # Optional document version.
  #     parameters: {}                           # Document parameters as a map of strings.
  #     schedule_expression: rate(7 days)        # Optional rate or cron expression.
  #     apply_only_at_cron_interval: false       # Optional; wait for schedule instead of running on apply.
  #     calendar_names: []                       # Optional SSM Change Calendar document ARNs/names.
  #     compliance_severity: MEDIUM              # CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, or UNSPECIFIED. Default: MEDIUM
  #     sync_compliance: AUTO                    # AUTO or MANUAL. Default: AUTO
  #     max_concurrency: "10%"                   # Optional node concurrency number or percentage.
  #     max_errors: "1"                          # Optional tolerated error number or percentage.
  #     automation_target_parameter_name: null   # Optional Automation target parameter.
  #     wait_for_success_timeout_seconds: null   # Optional provider wait timeout.
  #     targets:                                 # Up to five target blocks.
  #       - key: InstanceIds
  #         values: ["*"]
  #     output_location:                         # Optional command output destination.
  #       s3_bucket_name: existing-output-bucket # Required within output_location.
  #       s3_key_prefix: ssm-associations        # Optional S3 prefix.
  #       s3_region: us-east-1                   # Optional bucket Region.

  # Custom Patch Manager baselines.
  # patch_baselines:
  #   amazon_linux:                              # Arbitrary stable map key referenced by patch_groups.baseline_key.
  #     name: example-amazon-linux               # Default: <system-name>-<map-key>
  #     description: Security updates baseline   # Optional description.
  #     operating_system: AMAZON_LINUX_2         # AWS Patch Manager operating-system enum. Default: AMAZON_LINUX_2
  #     approved_patches: []                     # Optional explicit approved patch IDs.
  #     approved_patches_compliance_level: HIGH  # Optional compliance level for explicit approved patches.
  #     approved_patches_enable_non_security: false # Include approved non-security patches. Optional.
  #     rejected_patches: []                     # Optional explicit rejected patch IDs.
  #     rejected_patches_action: BLOCK           # ALLOW_AS_DEPENDENCY or BLOCK. Optional.
  #     available_security_updates_compliance_status: COMPLIANT # Optional COMPLIANT or NON_COMPLIANT.
  #     tags: {}                                 # Merged over the module standard tags.
  #     approval_rules:                          # Zero or more approval rules.
  #       - approve_after_days: 7                # Use this or approve_until_date as supported by AWS.
  #         approve_until_date: null             # ISO date, mutually exclusive with approve_after_days.
  #         compliance_level: HIGH               # CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFORMATIONAL, or UNSPECIFIED.
  #         enable_non_security: false           # Include matching non-security updates. Default: false
  #         patch_filters:                       # One to ten filters per rule.
  #           - key: CLASSIFICATION              # PRODUCT, CLASSIFICATION, MSRC_SEVERITY, PATCH_ID, SECTION, etc.
  #             values: [Security]
  #     global_filters:                          # Optional filters applied to every rule, maximum four.
  #       - key: PRODUCT
  #         values: [AmazonLinux2]
  #     sources:                                 # Optional alternative patch repositories, maximum twenty.
  #       - name: MyRepository
  #         products: [AmazonLinux2]
  #         configuration: "[main]\nname=Example\nbaseurl=https://example.invalid"

  # Patch group to baseline registrations.
  # patch_groups:
  #   amazon_linux:                              # Arbitrary stable map key.
  #     patch_group: amazon-linux                # Required value used by the instance Patch Group tag.
  #     baseline_key: amazon_linux               # Use exactly one: key from patch_baselines...
  #     # baseline_id: pb-0123456789abcdef0      # ...or an existing baseline ID managed elsewhere.

  # Shared Maintenance Window task role settings.
  maintenance:
    create_role: true                            # Create a role when at least one task exists. Default: true
    # role_name: example-ssm-maintenance-window  # Default: <short-system-name>-ssm-maintenance-window
    # role_path: /service-role/                   # IAM path, including leading/trailing slash. Default: /service-role/
    # additional_policy_arns: []                 # Extra task policies attached to the created role.

  # Maintenance Windows, registered targets, and RUN_COMMAND tasks.
  # maintenance_windows:
  #   monthly:                                   # Arbitrary stable window map key.
  #     name: example-monthly-patching           # Default: <system-name>-<window-key>
  #     description: Monthly approved patching   # Optional description.
  #     schedule: cron(0 3 ? * SUN#1 *)          # Required cron or rate expression.
  #     schedule_timezone: UTC                   # IANA timezone. Default: UTC
  #     schedule_offset: null                    # Optional number of days to offset cron execution.
  #     duration: 4                              # Window duration in hours. Default: 4
  #     cutoff: 1                                # Hours before the end when new tasks stop. Default: 1
  #     enabled: true                            # Enable the window. Default: true
  #     allow_unassociated_targets: false        # Allow task targets not registered with this window. Default: false
  #     start_date: null                         # Optional ISO-8601 start timestamp.
  #     end_date: null                           # Optional ISO-8601 end timestamp.
  #     tags: {}                                 # Merged over the module standard tags.
  #     targets:
  #       linux:                                 # Arbitrary target key referenced by tasks.target_keys.
  #         name: linux                          # Default: target map key
  #         description: Linux patch group       # Optional description.
  #         resource_type: INSTANCE              # INSTANCE or RESOURCE_GROUP. Default: INSTANCE
  #         owner_information: platform          # Optional owner information.
  #         targets:                             # One to five target selectors.
  #           - key: tag:Patch Group             # Examples: InstanceIds, tag:<key>, resource-groups:Name.
  #             values: [amazon-linux]
  #     tasks:
  #       install:                               # Arbitrary task map key.
  #         name: install-approved-patches       # Default: task map key
  #         description: Install approved patches # Optional description.
  #         task_arn: AWS-RunPatchBaseline       # RUN_COMMAND document name/ARN. Default: AWS-RunPatchBaseline
  #         task_type: RUN_COMMAND               # Only supported value. Default: RUN_COMMAND
  #         priority: 1                          # Lower numbers run first. Default: 1
  #         max_concurrency: "10%"               # Node concurrency number or percentage. Default: 10%
  #         max_errors: "1"                      # Tolerated error number or percentage. Default: 1
  #         cutoff_behavior: CANCEL_TASK         # CANCEL_TASK or CONTINUE_TASK. Default: CANCEL_TASK
  #         service_role_arn: null               # Required per task when maintenance.create_role is false.
  #         target_keys: [linux]                 # Required keys from this window's targets map.
  #         comment: Monthly patch installation  # Optional Run Command comment.
  #         document_version: "$LATEST"          # Optional command document version.
  #         output_s3_bucket: existing-output-bucket # Optional command output bucket.
  #         output_s3_key_prefix: maintenance    # Optional command output prefix.
  #         timeout_seconds: 3600                # Optional command timeout.
  #         parameters:                          # Run Command document parameters; values are string lists.
  #           Operation: [Install]
  #           RebootOption: [RebootIfNeeded]
  #         cloudwatch_output_enabled: true      # Optional Run Command CloudWatch output toggle.
  #         cloudwatch_log_group_name: /aws/ssm/maintenance # Default: the compliance Automation log group; this option references but does not create another group.
  #         notification_config:                 # Optional SNS Run Command notifications.
  #           notification_arn: arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:ssm-notifications
  #           notification_events: [All]         # All, InProgress, Success, TimedOut, Cancelled, or Failed.
  #           notification_type: Command         # Command or Invocation.
```

### Adoption notes

- Systems Manager allows only one apply-all Inventory association. Import it with
  `settings.inventory.existing_association_id`, disable Inventory, or retarget the existing association
  before enabling the module default. Direct Terraform/OpenTofu callers must declare the root import
  block or run the documented one-time import command.
- Default Host Management Configuration is account- and Region-scoped. Set
  `settings.default_host_management.create_role = false` to use an existing role with the configured
  name and path.
- `settings.document_security.block_public_sharing` defaults to `true`. The service setting blocks new
  public shares; it does not unshare an existing document.
- The default Automation log group uses `/aws/ssm/compliance-management/automation/<system-name>`,
  which is separate from the Session Manager module's `/aws/ssm/session-manager/audit-*` namespace.
  To reuse a centrally managed group instead, set `settings.automation_logging.create_log_group = false`
  and provide its name through `settings.automation_logging.log_group_name`.
- Maintenance Window `cloudwatch_log_group_name` overrides reference existing groups; this module only
  creates the Automation group controlled by `settings.automation_logging.create_log_group`.
- Maintenance Window tasks support `RUN_COMMAND` documents. They default to the AWS-managed
  `AmazonSSMMaintenanceWindowRole`; attach extra managed policies through
  `settings.maintenance.additional_policy_arns` when a task needs access to workload resources.
- Inventory resource data sync expects an existing S3 bucket and, when configured, KMS key. Their
  policies are outside this module because the destination may be centralized or cross-account.

## Quick Start

```sh
mkdir -p production/us-east-1/001/ssm-compliance-management
cd production/us-east-1/001/ssm-compliance-management

terragrunt scaffold github.com/cloudopsworks/terraform-module-aws-ssm-compliance-management
# Review the generated inputs.yaml, then:
terragrunt plan
terragrunt apply
```


## Examples

A patch-install Maintenance Window can target the same `Patch Group` value associated with a custom
baseline:

```hcl
settings = {
  maintenance_windows = {
    monthly = {
      schedule          = "cron(0 3 ? * SUN#1 *)"
      schedule_timezone = "UTC"
      duration          = 4
      cutoff            = 1

      targets = {
        amazon_linux = {
          targets = [{
            key    = "tag:Patch Group"
            values = ["amazon-linux"]
          }]
        }
      }

      tasks = {
        install = {
          task_arn        = "AWS-RunPatchBaseline"
          target_keys     = ["amazon_linux"]
          max_concurrency = "10%"
          max_errors      = "1"
          parameters = {
            Operation    = ["Install"]
            RebootOption = ["RebootIfNeeded"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Inputs

| Name | Description | Type | Default | Required |
| ---- | ----------- | ---- | ------- | :------: |
| <a name="input_extra_tags"></a> [extra\_tags](#input\_extra\_tags) | Extra tags to add to the resources | `map(string)` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_is_hub"></a> [is\_hub](#input\_is\_hub) | Is this a hub or spoke configuration? | `bool` | `false` | no |
| <a name="input_org"></a> [org](#input\_org) | Organization details | <pre>object({<br/>    organization_name = string<br/>    organization_unit = string<br/>    environment_type  = string<br/>    environment_name  = string<br/>  })</pre> | n/a | yes |
| <a name="input_settings"></a> [settings](#input\_settings) | AWS Systems Manager account and Region configuration for Security Hub CSPM controls SSM.1 through SSM.7; Session Manager resources are intentionally excluded | `any` | `{}` | no |
| <a name="input_spoke_def"></a> [spoke\_def](#input\_spoke\_def) | Spoke ID Number, must be a 3 digit number | `string` | `"001"` | no |

## Outputs

| Name | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| <a name="output_association_ids"></a> [association\_ids](#output\_association\_ids) | IDs of custom State Manager associations keyed by settings.associations key |
| <a name="output_automation_log_group_name"></a> [automation\_log\_group\_name](#output\_automation\_log\_group\_name) | CloudWatch Logs group configured for Systems Manager Automation customer-script logging |
| <a name="output_default_host_management_role_arn"></a> [default\_host\_management\_role\_arn](#output\_default\_host\_management\_role\_arn) | ARN of the module-created Default Host Management Configuration IAM role, or null when an existing role is used |
| <a name="output_document_arns"></a> [document\_arns](#output\_document\_arns) | ARNs of customer-owned, tagged Systems Manager documents keyed by settings.documents key |
| <a name="output_inventory_association_id"></a> [inventory\_association\_id](#output\_inventory\_association\_id) | ID of the AWS-GatherSoftwareInventory State Manager association |
| <a name="output_inventory_resource_data_sync_name"></a> [inventory\_resource\_data\_sync\_name](#output\_inventory\_resource\_data\_sync\_name) | Name of the optional Systems Manager Inventory resource data sync |
| <a name="output_maintenance_window_ids"></a> [maintenance\_window\_ids](#output\_maintenance\_window\_ids) | IDs of maintenance windows keyed by settings.maintenance\_windows key |
| <a name="output_maintenance_window_target_ids"></a> [maintenance\_window\_target\_ids](#output\_maintenance\_window\_target\_ids) | IDs of maintenance window targets keyed as window.target |
| <a name="output_maintenance_window_task_ids"></a> [maintenance\_window\_task\_ids](#output\_maintenance\_window\_task\_ids) | IDs of maintenance window tasks keyed as window.task |
| <a name="output_patch_baseline_ids"></a> [patch\_baseline\_ids](#output\_patch\_baseline\_ids) | IDs of custom patch baselines keyed by settings.patch\_baselines key |
| <a name="output_patch_scan_association_id"></a> [patch\_scan\_association\_id](#output\_patch\_scan\_association\_id) | ID of the non-rebooting AWS-RunPatchBaseline Scan association |
| <a name="output_security_hub_ssm_controls"></a> [security\_hub\_ssm\_controls](#output\_security\_hub\_ssm\_controls) | Module configuration status and Terraform resources supporting Security Hub CSPM controls SSM.1 through SSM.7 |
